Meshtastic Meshtastic lets compatible radios exchange messages and location information without cell service or internet access. Network: A distributed mesh where participating devices can relay messages. Dedicated repeaters are not required. Messaging: Group channels, direct messages, and location sharing. Common uses: Outdoor recreation, position reporting, community communication, and experimentation. Meshtastic Website MeshCore MeshCore lets compatible radios exchange messages directly or through a network of dedicated repeaters without cell service or internet access. Network: User devices communicate directly or through repeaters that forward messages along network paths. Messaging: Public channels, private messages, and optional room servers for stored messages. Common uses: Community messaging, fixed repeater networks, group coordination, and experimentation. MeshCore Website Meshtastic and MeshCore use LoRa technology but are separate systems. Devices require compatible firmware and radio settings to communicate. The Provo Auxiliary Communications Team (PACT) certification program is designed to prepare members for emergency operations through structured training and real-world participation. Participation is not required, but it is strongly encouraged. As members progress through certification levels, they develop increased confidence, technical proficiency, and familiarity with communication equipment and procedures. CERTIFICATION LEVELS LEVEL 1 Participant Basic readiness, radio setup, and participation in training nets. Learn & Participate → LEVEL 2 Support Consistent participation and ability to assist during PACT activities. Assist & Support → LEVEL 3 Independent Reliable independent operation during events, exercises, and activations. Operate & Execute → LEVEL 4 Leader Ability to lead teams and support coordination during operations. Lead & Coordinate ★ Tip: Each level builds on the previous one and increases your readiness and responsibility within PACT.

After completing all requirements for a certification level, email the PACT Membership Coordinator for verification. Once approved, your certification will be recorded and you will receive a signed certificate at the next quarterly interface meeting. Members are expected to maintain the equipment required for each certification level they have completed. While participation with other organizations is encouraged, only officially sponsored PACT activities count toward certification requirements. A list of qualifying events can be found on the Training Exercises & Events page. PACT’s certification program is similar to the UCARES certification requirements for those pursuing both programs.

Participating in community events gives PACT members valuable hands-on experience while serving their community. These volunteer opportunities help PACT members become more comfortable with their equipment, practice communication procedures, and develop skills that can be applied during emergencies.

The Provo City Half Marathon is an annual spring race held in Provo that attracts both beginner and experienced runners from across Utah and the surrounding region. Known for its fast, scenic downhill course, the race begins at South Fork Park in Provo Canyon and finishes in downtown Provo along University Avenue and Center Street. The course follows portions of the Provo River Parkway and offers runners views of the canyon, mountains, and river while descending nearly 900 feet over 13.1 miles. Organized by Run13, the event also includes a 5K and Kids Marathon and has become one of the fastest-growing races in Utah due to its PR-friendly course, energetic downtown finish, and strong community atmosphere.

The event typically utilizes approximately twenty amateur radio volunteers, including Net Control operators. Most volunteers are assigned to key race locations such as the start line, finish line, and water/aid stations along the course. Additional operators may be assigned as mobile or bike-mounted communicators to provide roving coverage throughout the event. Volunteer communications support for the Provo City Half Marathon is coordinated through Utah County Amateur Radio Emergency Service (UCARES). PACT members interested in participating should register through UCARES.

The America's Freedom Festival at Provo is one of the nation’s largest patriotic celebrations and has been a longstanding Provo tradition since the late 1800s. Held annually from spring through the Fourth of July, the festival features more than 25 community events, including the Grand Parade, Balloon Fest, and the nationally recognized Stadium of Fire. On Independence Day morning, thousands of spectators gather along University Avenue in downtown Provo to watch the Grand Parade, one of the festival’s most recognized community traditions.

The event typically utilizes approximately thirty-five amateur radio volunteers. Most volunteers are assigned to locations along the parade route, including the staging area and the parade start and finish lines. Several operators provide roving coverage throughout the event. All volunteers should plan on being at their assigned location by 0620. Volunteer communications support for the Freedom Festival Parade is coordinated through Utah County Amateur Radio Emergency Service (UCARES). PACT members interested in participating should register through UCARES.

Hike & Light the Y is a longstanding tradition that began in 1924. During Homecoming, BYU students, faculty, and alumni hike to the Y on Y Mountain and participate in a special lighting ceremony. Amateur radio volunteers help support the event by providing communications between the event organizers and key locations along the route.

The event typically utilizes fifteen amateur radio volunteers, including a Net Control operator. Most volunteers are stationed at key locations such as the trailhead, switchbacks, the top of the Y, and the shuttle pickup. Additional operators may be assigned as EMS or Director shadows to help relay information and coordinate requests for assistance throughout the event. Volunteers should be prepared for outdoor conditions, uneven terrain, and reduced visibility after sunset. Recommended equipment includes a reflective vest, flashlight or headlamp, an extra clothing layer, and an amateur radio with an earpiece. Volunteer communications support for Hike & Light the Y is coordinated through the BYU Amateur Radio Club (BARC). PACT members interested in participating should sign up through the club's leadership.

WEEKLY TRAINING NET Every Wednesday 8:30 PM · Mountain Time CHECK-INS 439.800 MHzSimplex ANNOUNCEMENTS & TRAINING Provo City Repeater Following Check-Ins ADD TO CALENDAR PACT holds a weekly training net to help its members practice radio procedures, build confidence, and stay familiar with emergency communication operations. While attendance is not required, regular participation is strongly encouraged.

The weekly training net is conducted in two phases. Members should remain on the assigned frequency until Net Control directs them to switch. 01 Check-Ins — Simplex Members check in by district on 439.800 MHz simplex, practicing the communication procedures used during PACT activations. ↓ 02 Announcements, Traffic & Training — Repeater After check-ins, Net Control directs stations to switch to the Provo City repeater for announcements, traffic, and training.
Members check in by district on 439.800 MHz simplex, practicing the communication procedures used during PACT activations.
After check-ins, Net Control directs stations to switch to the Provo City repeater for announcements, traffic, and training.

During the first portion of the net, Net Control will call for check-ins by each Provo Neighborhood District. When your district is called: Wait for a pause. State your FCC call sign slowly and clearly using standard phonetics. Indicate whether or not you have traffic for the net. Wait for acknowledgment from Net Control. Example Check-In​ NET CONTROL "All stations located in the North District, please check in." OPERATOR "This is November-Seven-Bravo-Yankee-Uniform with no traffic." If you have announcements, formal traffic, or information for the net, say "with traffic" instead of "with no traffic." After your check-in has been acknowledged, remain on 439.800 MHz simplex until Net Control instructs all stations to switch to the Provo City repeater. If you indicate that you have traffic, Net Control will let you know when to speak. Remember, PACT nets are directed nets. Operators should wait to be recognized by Net Control before transmitting unless there is emergency traffic. If you miss your district's check-in, wait until Net Control calls for late or missed check-ins.

The following guidance explains common situations members may encounter during the training net. Why Check-Ins Use Simplex PACT emergency operations primarily rely on simplex communications between operators and Net Control. Conducting weekly check-ins on simplex gives members regular practice using the same operating method that may be required during an activation. Because Provo covers a large geographic area, it is normal for some stations to hear Net Control but not every other station—or vice versa. After check-ins are complete, the net transitions to the Provo City repeater, allowing everyone to hear announcements, traffic, and the weekly training topic more reliably. Handling Doubles A double occurs when two or more stations transmit at the same time. When this happens, Net Control may not be able to clearly understand either station. If you hear a double: Stop transmitting. Wait for Net Control to identify a station or request a repeat. Do not try to continue over another station. Net Control may recognize part of a call sign and ask that station to transmit again. "The station ending in Bravo-Yankee-Uniform, please repeat your callsign." Brief pauses before transmitting help reduce doubles, especially during simplex check-ins.

PACT training nets follow a structured format as outlined below. Net Control Script Opening, district check-ins, announcements, training, and closing 10 Minutes Before the Net​ QST, QST, QST This is station ________ with an announcement for all stations monitoring this frequency. The Provo Auxiliary Communications Team Weekly Training Net will begin at 20:30 hours local time. Check-ins will be taken on 439.800 MHz simplex. After check-ins are complete, the remainder of the net will be conducted on the Provo City repeater. All stations interested in participating, please stand by until the net is called. 20:30 Hours — Start the Net​ Calling the Provo Auxiliary Communications Team Weekly Training Net. The purpose of this net is to provide training for amateur radio operators and to become familiar with radio equipment and emergency communication procedures in Provo. Check-ins will be taken on 439.800 MHz simplex. Once check-ins are complete, all stations will be directed to switch to the Provo City repeater for announcements, traffic, and tonight's training topic. This is a directed net. Please transmit ONLY as requested by Net Control. We use the ARRL standard word BREAK for priority or emergency traffic only. Is there any priority or emergency traffic for the net?
